head: cloud/tp2-control-hmac
title: fix(tp2): prove the control token by HMAC instead of sending it
body:
> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; an independent Claude Fable 5.1 review approved it before submission; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.

Test scope (CPU build/tests only, Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64 VM, GCC, `cmake --preset cpu-test`, no RDMA, no GPU): `cmake --build --preset pr` passes 42/42; `ctest -L tp2` (`tp_control_test`, `tp_instruction_latency_test`, `tp_executor_test`) passes 3/3. The new `tp_control_test` check fails on unpatched `rdma` (`FAIL: TP control hello does not carry the control token`) and passes with this change. The full CPU suite has the same 5 failures with and without the patch, all from a missing Python `numpy` in this VM (`h3_*_quality`, `serving_bench`, `qwen3_tts_reference_artifacts`, `qwen27b.tools`). `check-docs.py` passes. The three changed C++ files are clean under Ubuntu clang-format 18.1.3, not the Nix-pinned clang-format; with that version `check-format.py` still flags 22 files this PR does not touch. Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

## Problem

`TpControlChannel::Listen` binds the control port on all interfaces and accepts the first connection. `Handshake` then sends `--tp-control-token` in cleartext inside rank 0's hello, before it has read anything from the peer. Any host that can reach rank 0's control port while it waits for rank 1 can connect first and read the shared secret. It also blocks the pairing for that start.

## Change

- The hello now carries the same settings plus a fresh 32-byte random nonce in place of the token.
- After the hellos, the ranks exchange a `kAuth` frame. Its MAC is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the token, over a label, the sender's rank and both nonces, so a MAC only fits this connection and cannot be reflected back as the other rank's.
- Rank 1 proves the token first. Rank 0 checks it with `CRYPTO_memcmp` and sends its own proof only to a peer that proved the token. Otherwise it sends an empty refusal. Either way, a stranger connecting to rank 0 learns nothing about the token.
- A wrong token is still reported by name on both ranks ("control token"), next to any other setting that differs.
- `kVersion` goes from 19 to 20. As before, both ranks must run the same build.
- `gufo_tp_control` links `OpenSSL::Crypto`, which the build already requires.
- TP2.md says the channel is still not encrypted. Prompts and commands cross it in the clear, so the control port belongs on a trusted link. This change does not protect against an attacker who can sit in the middle of the connection.

## Tests

`tests/cli/tp_control_test.cpp`:
- Adds a `control token` case to the existing mismatch checks: both ranks refuse the pairing and name it.
- Adds a raw-socket stranger that connects to rank 0, reads its hello and checks that the token bytes are not in it. Rank 0's handshake must then fail.

Nightly hardware run: please pair two Strix Halo hosts on this build (Run section of TP2.md) and confirm they handshake and serve. A wrong `--tp-control-token` on one rank should name "control token" in both logs.

review.summary: Logic unchanged and correct, formatting now clean for all changed files, every body claim reproduced (tp_control_test, tp2 3/3, pr 42/42, check-docs), disclosure first and correct, no secrets or personal data; ready to publish.
